terms.meaning: a way to share values with many components without passing them one by one
a reference to the source that backs a statement
a pattern used to find and remove text, here old inline citation codes

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the React tools for sharing values and the types for the result and citations.
sections.why: Needed to build a shared citation context.

sections.name: CiteTarget
sections.title: Citation target shape
sections.what: Describes what the evidence panel needs for one source: its kind, label, project, text, status, source name, link, quoted passage and a note.
sections.why: Gives every kind of source one common shape so the panel can show them the same way.

sections.name: CiteCtx, Ctx
sections.title: Shared citation context
sections.what: Defines what the citation system offers to components below it: the number lookup, the description lookup, the open-evidence function and the current selection.
sections.why: Lets any marker find its number and details without passing them down by hand.

sections.name: walkCites
sections.title: Walking the deck for citations
sections.what: Looks through the deck and collects every citation id in the order they appear.
sections.why: The order is what gives each source its number.
sections.watch_out: It looks only for fields named cites, so a citation stored under another name is not counted.

sections.name: CiteProvider
sections.title: Building the citation register
sections.what: Creates the numbering from the deck order, prepares lookup tables for facts, findings, method items and sources, and returns functions that give a number or description for any id. Ids not yet numbered get a number on first request.
sections.why: Puts every citation in one register so numbers stay consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: Numbers for ids not in the deck are assigned when first asked for, so their numbers depend on the order in which the screen asks.

sections.name: useCites
sections.title: Using the citation context
sections.what: Gives a component access to the citation context and throws a clear error if it is used outside the provider.
sections.why: Makes a wiring mistake obvious during development.
sections.watch_out: The error stops the whole page rather than hiding only one marker.

sections.name: CiteMarks, stripMarkers
sections.title: Citation markers and cleanup of old text
sections.what: Draws each cited id as a small clickable number, highlighted when selected and marked when its source was unreachable. The cleanup function removes old inline codes such as bracketed fact ids from saved text.
sections.why: Gives readers a click target without making the prose unreadable, and hides codes left over in older saved results.
sections.watch_out: The cleanup works by pattern matching, so an unusual phrase that looks like a fact code could be removed by mistake.

sections.name: bareName
sections.title: Clean project names
sections.what: Removes bracketed curator notes from project names, such as a note about the operator, and tidies spacing.
sections.why: Lets names read cleanly where the notes are not wanted.
sections.watch_out: If a name is only a bracketed note, the original text is kept rather than returning an empty name.

sections.name: CitedText
sections.title: Text with citation markers
sections.what: Shows a cited statement with its markers and with any old inline codes removed.
sections.why: A single shared way to show any statement that has sources.

sections.name: CitedList
sections.title: Bulleted cited list
sections.what: Shows a list of cited statements as bullet points. Shows nothing when the list is empty.
sections.why: Used widely in the results, so the empty case is handled once.

summary: Builds the numbered source markers that appear next to statements in the Lessons Learnt results and the matching evidence panel.
purpose: Lets a reader click a small number next to a claim and see the fact, finding or method source behind it.
why: Likely reason: the exported PowerPoint uses the same numbering, so a number on screen points to the same source in the deck. Reason stated in a code comment.
how: `CiteProvider` walks the deck in order and gives each source the next number the first time it appears. It also looks up each source's details from the facts, findings and method items. `CiteMarks` draws the small numbered buttons. `CitedText` removes old inline citation text and adds the markers. `CitedList` puts cited statements in a bulleted list.
inputs: A `RecipeV3Result` object, the id of the selected source, and a function that opens the evidence panel.
outputs: Clickable number markers, bulleted cited lists, and a short description of each source for the evidence panel.
risks: If a citation id is not in the saved result, the marker still appears, marked as an unknown reference. Numbering depends on the deck walk order, so changing deck order changes the numbers.
debug: If a number points to the wrong source, compare the deck order with the walk in `CiteProvider`. If a marker says the reference is not in the saved result, the result is missing that item. If the page throws 'useCites outside CiteProvider', a component is drawn outside the provider.
